solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Put down date and location for game (6,5)

blocks.note: to squash a revolt is to put it down
to court someone is to date them

annotation.surface: Someone logging a fixture: noting the date and the venue for a match.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Put down date' reads as filling in a diary, but both words are verbs of a different kind: crushing and wooing.
annotation.definitionFit: A description by function: the walled indoor room where that racket sport is played is exactly a location for a game.

entries.clue: Evergreen, happy — and tidy (6,2)

blocks.note: the spruce is an evergreen conifer
feeling up = feeling happy

annotation.surface: A list of cheerful qualities, as if describing a person who is lively, happy and neat.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Evergreen' looks like an adjective describing a person who never ages; here it is a noun, the tree.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain phrasal-verb synonym: making a room or yourself neater and smarter is tidying.

entries.clue: Just rubbish bin used, article thrown in (8)

indicatorNotes.rubbish: rubbish letters are jumbled, badly arranged
indicatorNotes.thrown in: the article is tossed into the mix of letters

blocks.note: anagram fodder
the indefinite article, added to the fodder

annotation.surface: Someone complaining that a bin was used merely for rubbish, with some item tossed in.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Just rubbish bin' sounds like a scornful description; 'Just' is really the definition, the adjective meaning fair.
annotation.definitionFit: A just judge is an unbiased one: fair and impartial.

entries.clue: Dance while repeatedly spinning around leader in lambada (5)

indicatorNotes.repeatedly: something done repeatedly happens more than once, so the word is used twice over
indicatorNotes.spinning: a thing spinning turns about, so each copy is written back to front
indicatorNotes.around: the pair surrounds the next letter, placed one either side of it
indicatorNotes.leader in: the leader of a word is the letter at its front

blocks.note: as = while, turned round
its first letter
the second copy of AS, also turned round

annotation.surface: Dancers twirling again and again round the one leading the lambada.
annotation.walkthrough: The spinning and the lambada sit perfectly in the dance picture, so 'while' is easy to skip; it is the word that supplies AS, twice.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by category: this lively Latin American partner style, born in Cuban and Puerto Rican New York, belongs to the family of dances.

entries.clue: Bread invested in US state — money! (7)

indicatorNotes.invested in: put inside, like money invested in a business

blocks.note: Cal. is an abbreviation for California
pita is a flatbread, sitting inside CA…L

annotation.surface: Cash poured into an American state, 'bread' being slang for money.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Bread' is slang for money, which makes it look like the definition; it is literal bread, the pita. 'Invested' keeps the finance theme while meaning 'placed inside'.
annotation.definitionFit: Capital is money used to fund a business.

entries.clue: Find a little bureau near Thanet (7)

indicatorNotes.a little: only a small part of the words is used

blocks.note: the run starts with the last letter of bureau, takes all of near, and ends two letters into Thanet

annotation.surface: Someone tracking down a small office close to Thanet.
annotation.walkthrough: Thanet is an area on the Kent coast in England; the place name just provides letters: burea(U NEAR TH)anet.
annotation.definitionFit: Literally digging something out of the ground, used figuratively for discovering a fact or object that was buried or hidden.

entries.clue: Write date anew, current (9)

indicatorNotes.anew: the letters are written again in a new order

blocks.note: anagram fodder

annotation.surface: An instruction to re-date a document so that it is current.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Current' looks like an adjective meaning up to date, the natural goal of rewriting a date; it is the noun, a flow of water.
annotation.definitionFit: Tidewater is water moved by the tide, so a tidal current.

entries.clue: Lower allowance (3)

blocks.note: a verb here: to reduce, as prices are lowered
a noun: the share of the takings you are allotted

annotation.surface: Reducing someone's pocket money.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface reads 'Lower' as an adjective; it is a verb, and 'allowance' is a share of the takings.
annotation.definitionFit: A cut lowers something, and a cut is the portion you are allowed.

entries.clue: Preserve that valley (6)

blocks.note: to can food is to preserve it
yon = that (over there), old-fashioned

annotation.surface: A plea to protect a particular valley.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Preserve' reads as conservation; it is preserving in tins.
annotation.definitionFit: A canyon is a deep, steep-sided valley.

entries.clue: 11 in fit of pique (6)

blocks.note: points to the answer at 11 across, in its sense of disposition
an angry outburst, a tantrum

annotation.walkthrough: The cross-reference is to 11 across, CHARACTER: a person's temper is their temperament or character.
annotation.definitionFit: Temper means both a person's disposition and an angry outburst.

entries.clue: Revolting type with wind stifling belch, originally (5)

indicatorNotes.stifling: the first word smothers the second by surrounding it
indicatorNotes.originally: what a word is originally is how it begins, so take its first letter

blocks.note: to reel in a line is to wind it
first letter of belch, inside RE…EL

annotation.surface: A disgusting person trying to suppress a burp.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Revolting' and 'wind' paint a picture of bad manners; revolting means rising up in revolt, and wind is a verb.
annotation.definitionFit: A rebel is someone who revolts.

entries.clue: Spy one with Mudd? That’s not quite wrong! (9)

annotation.definition: Spy one with Mudd? That’s not quite wrong!

indicatorNotes.not quite: the word falls just short: its last letter goes
indicatorNotes.wrong: the letters are in the wrong order

blocks.note: anagram fodder
Mudd missing its final D

annotation.surface: The setter teasingly accusing himself of being a spy, then half taking it back.
annotation.walkthrough: Mudd is the setter's pen name, and a spy works under a false name too, so the whole clue, read straight, points at the answer while its words, one clipped, supply the letters.
annotation.definitionFit: Read whole, the clue says a spy and the setter Mudd have one thing in common that is not quite wrong: each goes by an assumed name.

entries.clue: Sort letter (9)

blocks.note: a noun here: a person, as in 'a decent sort'
a written symbol of an alphabet

annotation.surface: An instruction to file the post.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Sort letter' reads as a verb and object from a mail room; both words are nouns.
annotation.definitionFit: A character is both a kind of person and a written symbol.

entries.clue: Lecturer’s space full (5)

indicatorNotes.Lecturer’s: what a lecturer says is spoken, so the word is heard, not seen

blocks.note: a hole is an empty space

annotation.surface: A lecture hall with every seat taken.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Lecturer's' turns the next word into speech: a hole said out loud is heard as WHOLE.
annotation.definitionFit: Whole and full both mean complete, with nothing missing.

entries.clue: Tool let us in after some wiggling (7)

indicatorNotes.after some wiggling: the letters are wiggled around into a new order

blocks.note: anagram fodder

annotation.surface: A tool that finally opens a stuck door once it has been jiggled about.
annotation.walkthrough: The picture is picking a lock; the words 'let us in' are the letters themselves.
annotation.definitionFit: A utensil is a tool, especially one used in the kitchen.

entries.clue: Tool set with saucer to smash up (9)

indicatorNotes.to smash up: the words are broken up and reassembled

blocks.note: anagram fodder
anagram fodder

annotation.surface: A tool kit supplied along with a saucer for breaking things.
annotation.walkthrough: The crockery suggests a tea set being smashed; it is the letters of 'set' and 'saucer' that break.
annotation.definitionFit: Secateurs are a gardening tool, pruning shears.

entries.clue: Having consumed last of sangria, the drunk can’t stand (4)

indicatorNotes.Having consumed: the jumbled word swallows the letter
indicatorNotes.last of: the last of anything is its final part, here the closing letter
indicatorNotes.drunk: a drunk's letters stagger into a new order

blocks.note: THE jumbled
final letter of sangria, inside H…TE

annotation.surface: A drunk, having downed the last of the sangria, is unable to stay upright.
annotation.walkthrough: 'The drunk can't stand' is a complete picture of someone legless; 'can't stand' really means detest.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: saying you cannot stand someone means you loathe or detest them.

entries.clue: Lion, say, on a search for underground chamber (8)

indicatorNotes.on: in a down clue, one piece sits on top of the next

blocks.note: a lion is an example of a big cat
as printed
to comb an area is to search it thoroughly

annotation.surface: A lion on the hunt for an underground den.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Say' signals that lion is an example of something: a cat.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the Roman tunnels and vaults cut for burying the dead were underground chambers.

entries.clue: Good job, anything but rare! (4,4)

blocks.note: praise for a task
steak cooked right through, the opposite of bloody

annotation.surface: Praise for work that is anything but unusual.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Rare' reads as uncommon; it is the steak sense, barely cooked.
annotation.definitionFit: Well done is both congratulation and thoroughly cooked meat.

entries.clue: Dodge rogue, back away! (4)

indicatorNotes.back away: the back of the word goes away

blocks.note: a scamp is a rascal or rogue
the last letter, P, is removed

annotation.surface: A warning to dodge a villain and retreat.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Back away' sounds like retreating; it means the back of the word is removed. 'Dodge' is the noun, a swindle.
annotation.definitionFit: A dodge is a trick or swindle, which is a scam.

entries.clue: Hair parted by the explosive gas! (7)

indicatorNotes.parted by: the first word is split open by the second going into it
indicatorNotes.explosive: something explosive blows apart, scattering the letters of the word before it

blocks.note: a mane is a head of hair
THE blown apart, placed after the first letter of MANE

annotation.surface: Hair blown apart by an explosive gas.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Explosive gas' reads as one phrase and a natural definition, but 'explosive' is working on 'the'; the definition is 'gas' alone.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by category: the odourless fuel of natural gas and coal-mine firedamp is a gas.

entries.clue: Appropriate language ending in applause (7)

indicatorNotes.ending in: the ending of a word is its closing letter

blocks.note: a language
last letter of applause

annotation.surface: Fitting words that end a speech to clapping.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Appropriate language' reads as polite speech; 'Appropriate' is the definition on its own.
annotation.definitionFit: Germane means relevant, appropriate to the matter in hand.

entries.clue: Mannerly dope with blunted sword (7)

indicatorNotes.blunted: the sword loses its point, its first letter

blocks.note: dope and gen are both slang for information
steel (a sword) minus its first letter

annotation.surface: A polite fool fencing with a blade that has no point.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Dope' looks like an idiot; it is information, as is gen, British slang for the facts. Steel is a poetic word for a sword.
annotation.definitionFit: Genteel means polite and refined, mannerly.

entries.clue: 4 had been identified by hostilities? (6)

blocks.note: hostilities = war
past tense of see, in the sense of spotted or identified

annotation.walkthrough: The cross-reference is to 4 down, CAPITAL. Turn the passive round: 'was identified by hostilities' becomes 'hostilities identified it', with the verb after its subject.
annotation.definitionFit: Warsaw is the capital city of Poland.

entries.clue: Serious mix of lemons or melons (6)

indicatorNotes.mix of: a mix is a blend in which the ingredients lose their original arrangement

blocks.note: either word works: lemons and melons share the same six letters

annotation.surface: A grim-faced fruit salad.
annotation.walkthrough: The joke is that 'melons' is itself an anagram of 'lemons', so either fruit gives the same letters.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a grave, earnest face or occasion, with no levity in it.

entries.clue: A pedal for brewing (5)

blocks.note: as printed
pedal means relating to the foot

annotation.surface: A piece of kit used in making beer.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Brewing' suggests beer; it means developing, as in trouble brewing.
annotation.definitionFit: Something afoot is under way or brewing.

entries.clue: A viola playing after mass, unsuccessfully (2,2,5)

indicatorNotes.playing: a viola playing makes music, and the letters play into a new order
indicatorNotes.after: this piece comes after the other

blocks.note: a ton is a unit of mass
A VIOLA jumbled

annotation.surface: A viola played after a church mass, but in vain.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Mass' sounds religious, with music afterwards; it is the physics sense, weight.
annotation.definitionFit: To no avail means without success.

entries.clue: Poplar appearing, Scots pine evidently not, initially (5)

indicatorNotes.initially: initially means at the start, so each word gives its opening letter

blocks.note: first letters of appearing, Scots, pine, evidently, not

annotation.surface: A poplar showing up where a Scots pine clearly isn't.
annotation.walkthrough: The Scots pine is a decoy tree next to the real one: every word of it only lends its first letter.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by genus: the quaking tree, Populus tremula, with trembling leaves, belongs to that group of trees.

entries.clue: Gamble in rush to pen cryptic clue (9)

indicatorNotes.to pen: to pen animals is to shut them in an enclosure, so one word surrounds another
indicatorNotes.cryptic: the word is disguised, its letters jumbled

blocks.note: a spate is a rush or flood
CLUE jumbled, inside SP…ATE

annotation.surface: A setter taking a chance by dashing off a cryptic clue.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Pen' looks like writing; it means enclose.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym from finance: risking money on shares or property in hope of profit is a bet.

entries.clue: Still sweltering in centre of Napoli (5)

indicatorNotes.in: the first piece goes inside the second
indicatorNotes.centre of: the centre of a word is its middle, here the two innermost letters

blocks.note: middle two letters of Napoli
hot, inside P…O

annotation.surface: It is still baking hot in the middle of Naples.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Still' reads as an adverb, as in still hot; it is the noun, a still photograph.
annotation.definitionFit: A still is a single photograph, often from a film.

entries.clue: Some draw: I need — a better result? (3)

indicatorNotes.Some: only some of the letters are used

blocks.note: the last letter of draw, the lone I, and the first letter of need

annotation.surface: A player with a draw saying they need a better result.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Draw' sits in the surface as a match result, making victory the obvious improvement: dra(W I N)eed.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by comparison: set against the draw in the surface, victory ranks above a tie in any league table.

entries.clue: Test of verbal skills that would have wizard buzzing? (8,3)

blocks.note: the straight half: a contest in which words must be spelt aloud
read literally: a magician who casts charms, turned into the insect that buzzes

annotation.surface: A spelling contest that would get a gifted child excited.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Wizard' suggests a whizz-kid; read literally it is a magician, and a bee that casts spells is a 'spelling bee'.
annotation.definitionFit: A spelling bee is a contest testing how well competitors spell.
